$comment: Voice conversation turn-taking contract. Every client implements runVad, isEcho, reduce and displayState as pure functions (no IO, no clock, no randomness; time only comes from event atMs) and compares each case byte-exact with expected. vad: input.frames is run-length [[dBFS, frameCount], ...], expand before feeding. echo: compare echo exactly and overlap within 0.00005 (null when the transcript has no units). reduce: start from initialState(), fold input.events one by one; expected[i] is displayState, statusKey, the effect list and nextDeadlineMs after event i.

vad: Input is one dBFS value per frameMs frame. Clamp every value to frameDbClampDb first (NaN and -Infinity become -120). All arithmetic is IEEE-754 double in exactly the order written here.
floor starts at floorInitDb. It is updated only on non-voiced frames: floor = floor + floorAlpha * (db - floor), then clamped to floorClampDb.

Not speaking: a frame is voiced iff db >= floor + vadStartOverFloorDb and db >= vadAbsoluteMinDb. A non-voiced frame resets the pending voiced run. When the run reaches vadStartMs / frameMs frames (bargeInMinSpeechMs / frameMs in candidate mode), emit {type:speechStart, frame, prerollFrame} where frame is the first frame of the run and prerollFrame = max(0, frame - vadPrerollMs / frameMs); voicedMs starts at run length * frameMs.

Speaking: a frame is voiced iff db >= floor + vadContinueOverFloorDb (no absolute minimum). A voiced frame adds frameMs to voicedMs and resets the silence count. When vadEndSilenceMs / frameMs consecutive non-voiced frames are reached, emit at that frame index {type:speechEnd, frame, voicedMs} if voicedMs >= vadMinUtteranceMs, else {type:discarded, frame}; then go back to not speaking.

Candidate mode (barge-in candidate) applies only when opts.route is speaker and opts.playbackStartFrame is not null, and only to frames with index >= playbackStartFrame. Headphones and bluetooth never use candidate mode.

Grace frames are indexes playbackStartFrame .. playbackStartFrame + bargeInGraceMs / frameMs - 1 in candidate mode. They are skipped: no floor update, no voiced or silence counting, and a pending (not yet started) voiced run is reset to 0. A run crossing the end of the grace window starts at the first frame after it.

The end of the input emits nothing: an open utterance stays open (the host keeps feeding frames). Events are therefore strictly alternating speechStart then speechEnd|discarded, with non-decreasing frame numbers.
Audio sent to STT is frames prerollFrame .. speechEnd.frame inclusive (the trailing silence is included).
echo: isEcho(transcript, sentences) returns {echo, overlap}. sentences holds the previous sentence and the sentence currently playing (sentenceStarted events), whichever exist; their units are pooled into one multiset.

Units: normalize with NFKC, then full Unicode lowercase (locale-independent: JS toLowerCase, Kotlin lowercase(), Swift lowercased()). Walk code points (not grapheme clusters): a code point in \p{P}, \p{S}, \p{Z}, \p{Cc}, \p{Cf} or a variation selector (U+FE00..U+FE0F, U+E0100..U+E01EF) is a separator and is dropped; a code point inside a singleUnitRanges range (Han, kana, Hangul) is its own unit; every other maximal run of code points is one unit.
Separators split runs before they are removed: "hello world" is two units, "helloworld" is one.

hits = size of the multiset intersection of transcript units and the pooled sentence units. ratio = hits / transcriptUnits as a double. echo = ratio >= echoOverlapRatio (double comparison; 3/5 equals the literal 0.6). overlap = round(ratio * 10000) / 10000.
A transcript with zero units (empty, whitespace or punctuation only) is an echo with overlap null. With no sentences and a non-empty transcript, overlap is 0 and it is not an echo.
Fixtures avoid Greek capital sigma and Turkish dotted I, where platform lowercasing may differ.
state: initialState(): phase idle, route speaker, all flags false, counters 0, timestamps null. Phases: idle | listening | thinking | speaking | ended.

reduce(state, event) returns {state, effects}. It never mutates its input. Unknown event types, and every event while phase is ended, return the state unchanged with no effects. While phase is idle only start is accepted.
Every accepted-type event other than deadline sets lastActivityMs = atMs (even when the event is otherwise dropped).

A turn reset (on entering listening, and on entering thinking for a new turn) clears userSpeaking, playbackStopped, sttAttempts, awaitedUtteranceId, bargeIn, reply (none), drained, thinkingSinceMs, thinkingEarconPlayed, previousSentence and currentSentence. Entering listening also sets lastActivityMs = atMs; entering thinking sets thinkingSinceMs = atMs.

speakerBargeIn = route != speaker || !(deviceRemembersNoSpeakerBargeIn || falseBargeIns >= falseBargeInsPerConversation). It is recomputed on start, routeChanged and when the false barge-in limit is reached.

A reply is in flight from sendMessage until replyCompleted, replyFailed or cancelGeneration. The host must not forward events of a cancelled generation; the reducer additionally drops replySentence, replyCompleted and replyFailed when no reply is streaming.
events: start{route, deviceRemembersNoSpeakerBargeIn}: only from idle. Phase listening, effect startCapture. route is speaker | headphones | bluetooth (anything else is speaker).

VAD events (vadSpeechStart, vadSpeechEnd, vadDiscarded, bargeInDetected) are dropped while muted, interrupted, screenReaderSpeaking, messagePlaying, in phase thinking, and in phase speaking when !speakerBargeIn or a barge-in transcription is awaited.
vadSpeechStart: userSpeaking = true. vadSpeechEnd{utteranceId} and vadDiscarded are dropped unless userSpeaking; both set userSpeaking = false.

vadSpeechEnd in listening: enter thinking (turn reset), awaitedUtteranceId = utteranceId, sttAttempts = 1, effect transcribe{utteranceId}. In speaking with bargeIn: same awaited / attempts / transcribe, phase stays speaking. In speaking without bargeIn: nothing else.
vadDiscarded in speaking with bargeIn: bargeIn = false, effect resumePlayback{from:pausePoint} unless playbackStopped, then the finish check.
bargeInDetected: only in speaking, when userSpeaking and not already bargeIn. bargeIn = true, effect pausePlayback unless playbackStopped.
sttResult{utteranceId, text} and sttFailed{utteranceId} are dropped unless utteranceId == awaitedUtteranceId (late results after a cancel are ignored).

sttResult with bargeIn: isEcho(text, [previousSentence, currentSentence]). Echo: bargeIn = false, effect resumePlayback{from:sentenceStart} unless playbackStopped; only on route speaker falseBargeIns += 1, and when it reaches falseBargeInsPerConversation speakerBargeIn becomes false and effect rememberFalseBargeInConversation follows; then the finish check. Not echo: effects cancelGeneration, sendMessage{text}; enter thinking for a new turn with a streaming reply.
sttResult without bargeIn: text with zero echo units -> enter listening, no effect (not a failure). Otherwise effect sendMessage{text} (text unchanged), reply streaming, phase stays thinking.

sttFailed: if sttAttempts <= sttRetries then sttAttempts += 1 and effect transcribe{utteranceId}. Otherwise effects [cancelGeneration if bargeIn], speakPrompt{prompt:didNotCatch}, enter listening. Nothing is written to the pending-transcription slot.
replySentence{text}: only while the reply is streaming, in thinking or speaking. Phase speaking; unless playbackStopped: drained = false and effect enqueueSpeech{text}.
sentenceStarted{text} (host: a queued sentence began playing; feeds the echo check): only in speaking. previousSentence = currentSentence, currentSentence = text.
replyCompleted: reply completed; in thinking enter listening immediately, in speaking run the finish check. playbackDrained (queue empty): only in speaking; drained = true, then the finish check.

nextDeadlineMs(state): listening && !muted && !userSpeaking && !awaitingApproval && !interrupted && !screenReaderSpeaking && !messagePlaying -> lastActivityMs + idleTimeoutMs; thinking && !thinkingEarconPlayed && !awaitingApproval && !interrupted -> thinkingSinceMs + thinkingEarconMs; otherwise null. A deadline before it changes nothing; a deadline at or after it fires its rule.
Finish check: phase speaking && reply completed && (drained || playbackStopped) && !bargeIn -> enter listening.
replyFailed{code}: only while streaming. error = true, phase ended, effect endConversation{reason:error, code}.
approvalPending: accepted in any active phase. If not already set: awaitingApproval = true, effect speakPrompt{prompt:approvalNeeded}. approvalResolved clears it, no effect.

tapOrb: awaitingApproval -> nothing. muted && listening -> same as toggleMute. listening: effect forceEndUtterance if userSpeaking, else nothing. thinking: nothing while atMs - thinkingSinceMs < listenToThinkTapGuardMs (599 ignored, 600 acts), else effect cancelGeneration and enter listening. speaking: unless playbackStopped, playbackStopped = true, effect stopPlayback, then the finish check (text keeps generating; later sentences are not enqueued).
toggleMute: flip muted, effect setCaptureMuted{muted}. Muting clears userSpeaking (the open utterance is discarded by the host). Capture input is never closed.

deadline (host fires it once at nextDeadlineMs; there is no periodic tick): listening && !muted && !userSpeaking && !awaitingApproval && !interrupted && !screenReaderSpeaking && !messagePlaying && atMs - lastActivityMs >= idleTimeoutMs -> effects earcon{kind:end}, endConversation{reason:idle}, phase ended. thinking && !thinkingEarconPlayed && !awaitingApproval && !interrupted && atMs - thinkingSinceMs >= thinkingEarconMs -> effect earcon{kind:thinking}, once per turn.

interruptionBegan (if not already): interrupted = true, userSpeaking = false, effects [pausePlayback if speaking and !playbackStopped], pauseCapture. interruptionEnded (if set): interrupted = false; if speaking and !playbackStopped then playbackStopped = true and effect stopPlayback (playback never auto-resumes after a call); effect resumeCapture; then the finish check.
screenReaderSpeaking{speaking}: sets the flag; true also clears userSpeaking. VAD events are dropped while it is set.

routeChanged{route}: recompute speakerBargeIn. Leaving a private route (headphones / bluetooth) for speaker while speaking and !playbackStopped: playbackStopped = true, effect stopPlayback, then the finish check.

playMessage{messageId}: only in listening, not interrupted, not already playing. messagePlaying = true, userSpeaking = false, effects pauseCapture, playMessage{messageId}. messagePlaybackEnded (if playing): effect resumeCapture.
end{reason}: reason user | system (anything else is system). Effects [transcribeToDraft if reason user and userSpeaking], endConversation{reason}; phase ended.
display: displayState: error if error; null in idle or ended; else awaitingApproval; else muted if muted && phase listening; else the phase (listening | thinking | speaking).
statusKey = displayState, except speaking with route speaker and !speakerBargeIn -> speakingTapToInterrupt. Ids: listening, thinking, speaking, speakingTapToInterrupt, muted, awaitingApproval, error.
The UI reads only displayState / statusKey; it never derives state on its own.
host: The host turns real signals into events and executes effects in list order. cancelGeneration cancels the in-flight reply or transcription and discards its queued or paused speech.
rememberFalseBargeInConversation: the host counts such conversations per device; after conversationsToRemember of them it starts later conversations with deviceRemembersNoSpeakerBargeIn = true.

Page reachability (both engines): the voice bar on the home page only ever shows pageReachableStatusKeys.home; speaking always happens on the chat page because the host has already moved there (cascade: first sendMessage; realtime: first turn event, realtime-conversation rules.host).
Host only: create the chat on the first sendMessage from the home screen; ignore the voice button for stopToVoiceGuardMs after it turns back from stop.

Timers: no periodic tick. After every reduce the host reads nextDeadlineMs(state); when it differs from the armed value the host cancels the armed one-shot timer and, if non-null, arms one that dispatches deadline{atMs: now} once at that time (immediately when already past). It never polls. atMs uses one monotonic clock for all events.
